Rules / Tool

SK9026 --rules names an id no rule in this run can produce

--rules names one or more ids that no rule in this run can produce, alongside ids that can. The unknown ones contribute nothing to the report. Warning; the run continues and its exit code is unaffected. skala rules list names the allocated ids; repeat the option or separate ids with commas.

CategoryTool
Default severitywarning
ScopeCompilation
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileno — it reads the whole compilation
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

It exists because its absence read as a clean tree (#278): --rules SK3510,SK3511 bound a single string containing a comma, matched no rule, and exited 0 with no output — half an hour of an agent believing its analyzers were dead while they were fine. The comma is split now, but a mistyped id reaches the same false clean by another route, so the filter is checked against what actually loaded: the catalogue plus every loaded analyzer's supported diagnostics. A filter that is unknown in full is refused with exit 3 rather than reported here, because that run cannot produce a finding and its zero is not a measurement.

When it does not fire

A hosted analyzer whose SupportedDiagnostics getter throws is skipped, so its ids look unknown and a valid id can be reported here; that failure can widen the warning but never turn it into a refusal. Matching is case-insensitive.
